## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

// Start gameplay once without guessing between multiple controls or following links.
export async function startForCapture(page, { enabled = true, selector = '', timeout = 3000 } = {}) {
  if (!enabled) return { clicked: false, reason: 'disabled' }
  const candidate = selector
    ? page.locator(selector)
    : page.locator('button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], [role="button"]')
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout
  do {
    const matches = []
    for (const control of await candidate.all()) {
      if (!await control.isVisible() || !await control.isEnabled()) continue
      const eligible = await control.evaluate((element, explicit) => {
        if (element.closest('a[href], form') || element.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') return false
        if (explicit) return true
        const label = element.getAttribute('aria-label') || element.value || element.textContent || ''
        return /^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i.test(label.trim())
      }, Boolean(selector))
      if (eligible) matches.push(control)
    }
    if (matches.length > 1) return { clicked: false, reason: 'ambiguous' }
    if (matches.length === 1) {
      try { await matches[0].click({ trial: true, timeout: 2000 }) }
      catch (error) {
        if (error.name === 'TimeoutError') return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-actionable' }
        throw error
      }
      await matches[0].click({ timeout: 2000, noWaitAfter: true })
      return { clicked: true }
    }
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) break
    await page.waitForTimeout(Math.min(200, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())))
  } while (Date.now() <= deadline)
  return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-found' }
}

fi
ready=false

  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then

  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done

/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.

    fi

    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then

    exit 1

Let's design game depth carefully so it's actually fun.

Coordinate system: x across width, z along length. Pitch: width 40, length 62? Small pitch for 3v3. Attack along z. Team A (home) attacks +z, defended goal at z=-L/2. Team B attacks -z. Use width X, length Z.

Camera: broadcast-ish behind home team? For mobile, follow ball from the side at height ~16, behind the attacking direction? A dynamic camera positioned behind the player's team goal looking forward (like FIFA) gives intuitive controls (up = forward). But when defending, camera flips? That's disorienting. Standard football games use side-view or behind-player. On phone, behind-player camera with joystick relative to camera is intuitive. Use camera behind ball/controlled player orientation toward opponent goal, with rotation smoothing. Or fixed orientation along +z (home attacking +z): camera at (controlled.x*0.3, 18, controlled.z - 22) looking at ball ahead. This keeps up=+z. When you switch to defending, still camera behind (toward own goal) means you're looking toward your own goal? Hmm.

Alternative: side-on broadcast camera fixed on sideline at x = -something, looking across pitch, joystick up/down maps to z, left/right maps x. This is classic and works well both attack/defense, showing whole pitch and goals left/right. But "insane dribbling" visibility better behind-player.

I think dynamic camera behind ball with direction of play: home attacks +z always (human always home), camera positioned at z = ball.z - 26, looking at ball + forward offset, with slight x offset. When you defend, you're facing your own goal (camera behind you), controls relative to view. It works like most 3D sports games. But if you turn around with the ball to pass back, camera stays. Fine.

Actually camera behind the player with view toward +z, and human team always attacks +z. Camera z = min(player.z - 24, ...). Clamp so you can see goal. If player goes near opponent goal, camera at z=player.z-22. If ball behind player? Camera tracks ball mostly. Let camera target = blend(controlled, ball), camera position = target - (0, -height, distance) in z, so looking up-pitch. For defending near own goal, view shows your keeper and own goal, good.

Add camera side offset x = controlled.x * 0.35 and lookAt x = ball.x * 0.5. Slight dynamic FOV kick on sprint.

Mobile performance: 8 players × ~10 meshes = fine. Stadium crowd: use instanced boxes ~2000 with simple colors. Grass: one plane with procedural canvas texture stripes. Nets: line segments.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D 3v3 street-football game demo for phone/tablet with insane dribbling, great shooting, selectable playstyles, and bots to play against.
- Deliver working code in the repo, verify in browser with screenshots, and note assumptions only when finished.

## Requirements
- 3D game, 3v3, phone/tablet first, responsive touch controls.
- Insane dribbling, great shooting, and playstyles.
- Demo must be immediately playable, with bots on the opposing team.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Screenshots for self-checks should be small JPEGs (max 1280px wide) and only the latest should be inspected.

## Decisions
- Stack: vanilla JS + Three.js + Vite, with custom 2.5D physics rather than a physics engine.
- Match format: 2:00 clock, first to 5 goals, golden goal if tied at 0:00.
- 3 outfield players plus an AI goalkeeper per team; human controls one NEON outfield player, auto-switch to ball carrier/nearest defender.
- Four team playstyles: SHOWMAN, SNIPER, ENGINE, ANCHOR; three bot difficulties: CASUAL, PRO, LEGEND.
- Shooting: hold-to-charge, release in a green “perfect” zone, aim assist + curl; sprint+pass = lofted through ball.
- Controls: virtual floating-ish fixed joystick bottom-left; PASS/SKILL/SPRINT/SHOOT buttons bottom-right; keyboard WASD, SPACE, K, J, SHIFT, ESC; gameplay camera fixed-looking up-pitch for intuitive phone controls.
- Stadium aesthetic: neon night street-football arena, boards, crowd, floodlights, net meshes, animated confetti/particles, procedural audio.
- Menu CTA has `aria-label="Play"` so capture auto-start clicks it despite sub-label text.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` (three ^0.187.0, vite ^8.3.7), Vite build succeeds.
- Full UI/HTML/CSS: main menu with playstyle cards, difficulty picker, Play CTA, HUD/scorebug, pause, end screen, goal flash, toasts, touch controls, responsive portrait/landscape rules.
- Three.js stadium/pitch/goals/nets/ads/crowd/floodlights/sky/city/lighting implemented.
- Ball, players, effects, input, audio, AI, match engine, cameras, rules, game flow, debug hook `window.NEON` implemented.
- Local dev server running in tmux session `neon` at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`.
- Browser smoke test passes with zero page errors; menu auto-start via Play works; game enters `play`, home striker NOVA owns ball.
- Mobile screenshots saved: `screenshots/menu-mobile.jpg`, `screenshots/play-mobile.jpg`; both render properly.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay polish and deeper playtesting. Current mobile gameplay view looks dark/flat near own half: large dark foreground, signage partially clipped, player models readable but small, neon atmosphere weaker than intended.
- Need desktop and landscape screenshots, simulate movement/shot/goal/pause/end states, and verify controls, AI, keeper saves, scoring and reset flows.
- Need mobile menu layout polish: bottom empty space; style perks hidden on mobile.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run Playwright at desktop (1280×800) and mobile landscape; inspect latest JPEG screenshots.
2. Exercise keyboard/touch movement, charged shot, pass, skill/tackle, goal scoring, goal celebration, kickoff reset, pause, and end overlay; capture any runtime errors from `page.on('pageerror')`.
3. Improve visuals: brighten pitch/foreground, make menu background more legible, fix sign clip/placement, show playstyle perks on mobile, reduce empty menu bottom space.
4. Tune gameplay feel from observed telemetry (ball control distance, AI pressure, shot speed, keeper saves, camera framing).
5. Verify production build and default `start.sh`/capture flow, then save fresh final JPEG screenshots and summarize assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/game.js`: core match loop, input, shooting/passing, physics, rules, camera, HUD data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/ai.js`: AI decisions, goalkeeper positioning/dive/save/distribution.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/player.js`: player models, animation, movement, skill/slide, stamina.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/ball.js`: ball texture/physics/trail/dribble placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/pitch.js`: stadium, pitch markings, goals/nets, stands, crowd, lights.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/constants.js`: field/match dimensions, teams, playstyles, difficulty, formations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/effects.js`: GPU particle bursts, confetti, shock rings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/input.js`: touch joystick/buttons, keyboard, gamepad.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio kicks, whistle, crowd, save, UI sounds.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: DOM screen/HUD bindings and overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: renderer/scene boot, UI callbacks, resize, main loop, `window.NEON`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: all screens, HUD, menu, touch button markup.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D 3v3 street-football game demo for phone/tablet with insane dribbling, great shooting, selectable playstyles, and bots to play against.

## Requirements
- 3D game, 3v3, phone/tablet first, responsive touch controls.

- Demo must be immediately playable, with bots on the opposing team.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

- Stack: vanilla JS + Three.js + Vite, with custom 2.5D physics rather than a physics engine.

- Shooting: hold-to-charge, release in a green “perfect” zone, aim assist + curl; sprint+pass = lofted through ball.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
